title: How Small Can You Go? A Controlled Study of LoRA Rank, Target Modules, and Quantization Trade-offs for Text-to-SQL on a 60M-Parameter Model

images.desc:
5.4  Pareto Analysis


Figure 1 plots exact-match accuracy against trainable parameters
and peak training memory. The Pareto-optimal configuration under either budget is
LoRA r=16r{=}16 on {q,v}\{q,v\}: 59.6% exact-match with 589,824 trainable
parameters (0.97% of total) and 1.60 GB peak memory, recovering 83.7% of full
fine-tuning accuracy at 31% lower memory cost and 1% of the parameter count.
The zero-shot baseline confirms that task-specific adaptation is essential.


Figure 1: Accuracy vs. trainable parameters (left) and vs. peak training
memory (right). Up-and-left is better in both plots. LoRA r=16r{=}16 on
{q,v}\{q,v\} lies on the Pareto front in both panels, offering the best
accuracy-per-parameter and accuracy-per-memory trade-off among all
configurations evaluated.

Table 3: Exact-match accuracy across three random seeds. Mean and standard
deviation are computed over seeds 42, 123, and 456. Lower-rank configurations
show higher variance (LoRA r=2r{=}2: std=0.063), while quantized configurations
are notably stable (QLoRA INT8: std=0.006, QLoRA NF4: std=0.015).


The rank ordering of configurations is consistent across all three seeds:
full fine-tuning >> LoRA r=32r{=}32 ≈\approx LoRA r=16r{=}16 >> LoRA
r=8r{=}8 >> LoRA r=4r{=}4 >> LoRA r=2r{=}2. Lower ranks show higher
variance (std up to 0.063 for r=2r{=}2), suggesting sensitivity to
initialization at minimal parameter budgets. QLoRA configurations are
among the most stable, with std of 0.006 (INT8) and 0.015 (NF4),
likely because quantization regularizes the optimization landscape.


The Pareto plots for all three seeds are shown in
Figures 1, 2, and 3.
The consistent clustering of configurations across seeds confirms that
the efficiency trade-offs identified in Section 5 are robust to
random initialization.


Figure 2: Pareto efficiency plots for seed 123. Configuration ranking and
clustering patterns are consistent with seed 42 (Figure 1).


Figure 3: Pareto efficiency plots for seed 456. The rank ordering and
Pareto front are consistent across all three seeds, confirming robustness
of the reported trade-offs.


Execution accuracy caveat.


Execution accuracy is computed using an in-process SQLite engine over the
subset of evaluation examples where the gold SQL was executable (25 of 500,
i.e. 5% of the evaluation set). This small executable subset means
execution accuracy estimates carry high variance and should be interpreted
with caution. Exact-match accuracy over the full 500 examples is the more
reliable metric throughout this study.
